openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-01-03.title: Cell Membrane
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-01-03.caption: The cell membrane of the cell is a phospholipid bilayer containing many different molecular components, including proteins and cholesterol, some with carbohydrate groups attached.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-01-03.alt: This image shows a lipid bilayer with different types of proteins, lipids and cholesterol embedded in it.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-01-03.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Cell Membrane”, section 3.1 The Cell Membrane. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-02-03.title: Golgi Apparatus
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-02-03.caption: (a) The Golgi apparatus manipulates products from the rough ER, and also produces new organelles called lysosomes. Proteins and other products of the ER are sent to the Golgi apparatus, which organizes, modifies, packages, and tags them. Some of these products are transported to other areas of the cell and some are exported from the cell through exocytosis. Enzymatic proteins are packaged as new lysosomes (or packaged and sent for fusion with existing lysosomes). (b) An electron micrograph of the Golgi apparatus.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-02-03.alt: This figure shows the structure of the Golgi apparatus. The diagram in the left panel shows the location and structure of the Golgi apparatus. The right panel shows a micrograph showing the folds of the Golgi in detail.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-02-03.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Golgi Apparatus”, section 3.2 The Cytoplasm and Cellular Organelles. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-02-05.title: Peroxisome
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-02-05.caption: Peroxisomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain an abundance of enzymes for detoxifying harmful substances and lipid metabolism.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-02-05.alt: This diagram shows a peroxisome, which is a vesicular structure with a lipid bilayer on the outside and a crystalline core on the inside.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch03-02-05.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Peroxisome”, section 3.2 The Cytoplasm and Cellular Organelles. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch19-04-03.title: Platelets
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch19-04-03.caption: Platelets are derived from cells called megakaryocytes.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch19-04-03.alt: This flowchart shows a myeloid stem cell differentiating into platelets.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch19-04-03.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Platelets”, section 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-03-01.title: Mouth
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-03-01.caption: The mouth includes the lips, tongue, palate, gums, and teeth.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-03-01.alt: This diagram shows the structure of the mouth. The teeth, lips, tongue, gums and many other parts are labeled.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-03-01.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Mouth”, section 23.3 The Mouth, Pharynx, and Esophagus. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-03-07.title: Esophagus
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-03-07.caption: The upper esophageal sphincter controls the movement of food from the pharynx to the esophagus. The lower esophageal sphincter controls the movement of food from the esophagus to the stomach.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-03-07.alt: This diagram shows the esophagus, going from the mouth to the stomach. The upper and the lower esophageal sphincter are labeled.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-03-07.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Esophagus”, section 23.3 The Mouth, Pharynx, and Esophagus. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-04-01.title: Stomach
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-04-01.caption: The stomach has four major regions: the cardia, fundus, body, and pylorus. The addition of an inner oblique smooth muscle layer gives the muscularis the ability to vigorously churn and mix food.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-04-01.alt: This image shows a cross-section of the stomach, and the major parts: the cardia, fundus, body and pylorus are labeled.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-04-01.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Stomach”, section 23.4 The Stomach. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-05-01.title: Small Intestine
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-05-01.caption: The three regions of the small intestine are the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-05-01.alt: This diagram shows the small intestine. The different parts of the small intestine are labeled.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-05-01.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Small Intestine”, section 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-05-04.title: Large Intestine
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-05-04.caption: The large intestine includes the cecum, colon, and rectum.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-05-04.alt: This image shows the large intestine; the major parts of the large intestine are labeled.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-05-04.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Large Intestine”, section 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-06-04.title: Gallbladder
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-06-04.caption: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile, and releases it into the two-way cystic duct when it is needed by the small intestine.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-06-04.alt: This figure shows the gallbladder and its major parts are labeled.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch24-06-04.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Gallbladder”, section 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

openstax-ap2e-fig-ch26-04-01.title: Podocytes
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch26-04-01.caption: Podocytes interdigitate with structures called pedicels and filter substances in a way similar to fenestrations. In (a), the large cell body can be seen at the top right corner, with branches extending from the cell body. The smallest finger-like extensions are the pedicels. Pedicels on one podocyte always interdigitate with the pedicels of another podocyte. (b) This capillary has three podocytes wrapped around it.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch26-04-01.alt: The left panel of this figure shows an image of a podocyte. The right panel shows a tube-like structure that illustrates the filtration slits and the cell bodies.
openstax-ap2e-fig-ch26-04-01.credit: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax. Figure “Podocytes”, section 25.4 Microscopic Anatomy of the Kidney. CC BY 4.0. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction
